editorial:
If you love music biopics with heart and sparkle, Rocketman is a wild ride through Elton John's life. The film follows young Reginald Dwight as he grows from a shy piano prodigy into the flamboyant superstar Elton John. Along the way, you watch him struggle with fame, family, and his own identity while writing hits with lyricist Bernie Taupin. The vibe is colorful, emotional, and packed with big musical numbers that feel like a Broadway show mixed with a rock concert.

Taron Egerton absolutely nails the role, singing and dancing his way through Elton's biggest songs. The costumes are stunning, and the fantasy-style musical scenes keep things fresh. On the downside, the story can feel a bit rushed in places, and some darker moments get glossed over. Still, if you enjoy music movies or biopics, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Elton checks into rehab and faces his past, including his difficult relationship with his parents and his manager. He embraces sobriety and accepts himself fully. The movie ends with him performing "I'm Still Standing" as a confident, sober man, showing that he survived the chaos and came out stronger on the other side.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music biopics, Elton John fans, and viewers who enjoy colorful, emotional stories about overcoming personal struggles.
